questions.q:
For combustion of one mole of magnesium in an open container at $300K$ and $1$~bar pressure, ${Δ}_{C}H^{⊖} = - 601 . 70kJ{mol}^{- 1}$, the magnitude of change in internal energy for the reaction is $kJ$. (Nearest integer)
(Given : $R = 8 . 3JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$Mg\left(s\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2\left(G\right)} ⟶ MgO\left(S\right){ΔH}_c^{°} = - 601 . 70KJ / Mole$

$\Delta H ° = \Delta U + \Delta ngRT$

$- 601 . 70 = \Delta U + \left[\left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times 8 . 3 \times 300\right] \times {10}^{- 3}$

$- 601 . 7 = \Delta U - 1 . 245$

$\Delta U = - 599 . 455KJ$

\left|\Delta U\right| = 599 . 455KJ \approx 600$

$

questions.q: The reaction of cyanamide, ${NH}_{2}CN  \left(s\right)$ with oxygen was run in a bomb calorimeter and $\Delta U$ was found to be $- 742 . 24kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ . The magnitude of ${ΔH}_{298}$ for the reaction ${NH}_{2}CN\left(s\right) + $\dfrac{3}{2}{O}_{2  \left(g\right)} \to {N}_{2 \left(g\right)} + {O}_{2\left(g\right)} + {{H}_{2}O\left(l\right)$~is~$kJ$. (Rounded off to the nearest integer) [Assume ideal gases and $R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$]$

questions.solution:
$\Delta H = \Delta U + {Δn}_{g}RT$

$= - 742 . 24 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{8 . 314}{1000} \times 298$

$= - 741kJ / mol$

Hence answer is \left(741\right)$

$

questions.q: For a certain thermochemical reaction $M \to N$ at $T = 400K, {ΔH}^{o} = 77 . 2kJ{mol}^{- 1}, {ΔS}^{o} = 122{JK}^{- 1}$, $log$ equilibrium constant $( logK )$ is $-$ _____\times {10}^{- 1}.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given,

$T = 400K, {ΔH}^{o} = 77 . 2kJ{mol}^{- 1}, {ΔS}^{o} = 122{JK}^{- 1}$

${ΔG}^{o} = {ΔH}^{o} - {TΔS}^{o}$

$= 77 . 2 \times {10}^{3} - 400 \times 122 = 28400J$

$\Delta G ° = - 2 . 303RTlogK$

Where K is the equilibrium constant.

By putting the values in above equation,

$⇒ 28400 = - 2 . 303 \times 8 . 314 \times 400 \times logK$

$⇒ logK = - 3 . 708 = - 37 . 08 \times {10}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
An ideal gas, (\overline{\mathrm{C}}_{\mathrm{v}}=$\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{R}$), is expanded adiabatically against a constant pressure of 1 atm untill it doubles in volume. If the initial temperature and pressure is (298 $\mathrm{~K}$) and (5 $\mathrm{~atm}$), respectively then the final temperature is _______ ($\mathrm{K}$) (nearest integer).
[(\overline{\mathrm{C}}_{\mathrm{v}}) is the molar heat capacity at constant volume]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{U}=\mathrm{q}+\mathrm{w}(\mathrm{q}=0) \\ & \mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{V}} \Delta \mathrm{T}=-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{ext}}\left(\mathrm{V}_2-\mathrm{V}_1\right) \\ & \mathrm{V}_2=2 \mathrm{~V}_1 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{nRT}_2}{\mathrm{P}_2}=\frac{2 \mathrm{nRT}_1}{\mathrm{P}_1} \\ & \mathrm{P}_1=5, \mathrm{~T}_1=298 \\ & \mathrm{P}_2=\frac{5 \mathrm{~T}_2}{2 \times 298} \\ & \mathrm{n} \frac{5}{2} \mathrm{R}\left(\mathrm{T}_2-\mathrm{T}_1\right)=-1\left(\frac{\mathrm{nRT}_2}{\mathrm{P}_1}-\frac{\mathrm{nRT}_1}{\mathrm{P}_1}\right) \end{aligned}$
Put $\mathrm{T}_1=298$ and $\mathrm{P}_2=\frac{5 \mathrm{~T}_2}{2 \times 298}$ Solve and we get $T_2=274.16 \mathrm{~K}\mathrm{T}_2 \approx 274 \mathrm{~K}$

questions.q: When a $60W$ electric heater is immersed in a gas for $100s$ in a constant volume container with adiabatic walls, the temperature of the gas rises by $5 ° C$. The heat capacity of the given gas is ${JK}^{- 1}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\text{Heat capacity} = \dfrac{ Heat absorbed }{ change in temperature }$

1 Watt = 1 Joule per second

Hence, heat absorbed~$= 60 \times 100J$

Change in temperature~$= 5 ° C$

Heat capacity$= \dfrac{60 \times 100J}{5}$

$= 1200{JK}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
The value of $logK$ for the reaction~$A ⇌ B$~at $298K$ is _______ .$~(Nearest integer)

Given:~$\Delta H ° = - 54 . 07kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

$\Delta S ° = 10{JK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$

(Taken~$2 . 303 \times 8 . 314 \times 298 = 5705 )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We can use the relationship between the equilibrium constant ($K$) and the standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G °$) to calculate the value of $logK$ at $298K$

Given,

$∆ H^{o} = – 54 . 07kJ{mol}^{– 1} ∆ S^{o} = 10{JK}^{– 1}{mol}^{– 1}$

We know,~

$∆ G ° = ∆ H ° - T ∆ S °$

$= - 54 . 07 - \dfrac{298 ( 10 )}{1000}$

$= - 57 . 05kJ / mole$

$∆ G ° = - 2 . 303RT{logK}_{eq }$

$- 57 . 05 \times 1000 = - 2 . 303 \times 8 . 314 \times 298{logK}_{eq }$

$- 57 . 05 \times 1000 = - 5705\log_{\mathrm{eq}}$

$10 = {logK}_{eq }$

;

questions.q:
When $600mL$ of $0 . 2M{HNO}_{3}$ is mixed with $400mL$ of $0 . 1MNaOH$ solution in a flask, the rise in temperature of the flask is_____\times {10}^{- 2} ° C$
(Enthalpy of neutralisation~$= 57kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ and Specific heat of water $= 4 . 2{JK}^{- 1}g^{- 1}) (Neglect heat capacity of flask)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Number of moles of given acid and base are

{HNO}_{3} = $\dfrac{600}{1000} \times$0 . 2M = 0 . 12moles
NaOH = $\dfrac{400}{1000} \times$0 . 1M = 0 . 04moles$

Now neutralisation reaction between them will be

${HNO}_{3} + NaOH \to {NaNO}_{3} + {H}_{2}O0 . 12mole0 . 04mole0 . 08mole0mole0 . 04mole$

Heat relesed during this reaction will be~

${Δ}_{r}H = 0 . 04 $\times \left(57 \times {10}^{3}\right)J$

$= 2280J$

Now temperature increased can be calculated by

$mS \Delta T = 2280J$

$⇒ 1000mL \times \dfrac{1gm}{mL} \times4 . 2 \times \Delta T = 2280$

$\Delta T = \dfrac{2280}{4 . 2} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 542 . 86 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$\Delta T = 54 . 286 \times {10}^{- 2}° C$

questions.q: $4 . 0L$ of an ideal gas is allowed to expand isothermally into vacuum until the total volume is $20L$. The amount of heat absorbed in this expansion is $L$ atm.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In case of expansion, work is done by system.

Now, as we know that,

$W = - {P}_{ext .} ∆ V$

As the gas is expanding into~vacuums which has no pressure, i.e.,

${P}_{ext .} = 0$

$∴ W = 0$

Hence, no work is done.

From first law of thermodynamics,

$\Delta U = q + W$

As the system is working at constant temperature, i.e., isothermally.

$∴ \Delta U = 0$

Hence~$q = - W = 0$

questions.q:
Five moles of an ideal gas at $293K$ is expanded isothermally from an initial pressure of $2 . 1MPa$~to $1 . 3MPa$~against at constant external pressure $4 . 3MPa$. The heat transferred in this process is ___~${kJmol}^{- 1}$. (Rounded-off to the nearest integer)

[ Use $R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$n = 5, T = 293K = const, \Delta U = 0$

${P}_{1} = 2 . 1MPa, {P}_{2} = 1 . 3MPa$

${P}_{ext} = 4 . 3MPa = const .$

$W = - {P}_{ext} \left({V}_{2} - {V}_{1}\right) = - {P}_{ext}\left(\dfrac{nRT}{P2} - \dfrac{nRT}{P1}\right)

or, $W = - {P}_{ext}nRT \left(\dfrac{1}{P2} - \dfrac{1}{P1}\right)$

$= - 4 . 3 \times 5 \times 8 . 314 \times 293 \left(\dfrac{1}{1 . 3} - \dfrac{1}{2 . 1}\right)

$= - 4 . 3 $\times$5 $\times$8 . 314 $\times$293 \left(\dfrac{2 . 1 - 1 . 3}{1 . 3 \times 2 . 1}\right)$

$= - 15347 . 7J$

or, $W = - 15 . 35kJ$

$\Delta U^{0} = q + W$

$∴ q = - W$

or, $q = 15 . 35kJ$ (for $5$ moles)

$∴ q / mole = \dfrac{15 . 35}{5} = 3kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

questions.q:
$0 . 3g$ of ethane undergoes combustion at $27 ° C$ in a bomb calorimeter. The temperature of calorimeter system (including the water) is found to rise by $0 . 5 ° C$. The heat evolved during combustion of ethane at constant pressure is ${kJmol}^{- 1}$.
(Nearest integer)

[Given : The heat capacity of the calorimeter system is $20kJK^{- 1}, R = 8 . 3{JK}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$.
Assume ideal gas behaviour.

Assume ideal gas behaviour.

Atomic mass of $C$ and $H$ are $12$ and $1g{mol}^{- 1}$ respectively]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The bomb calorimeter is an instrument used to measure the heat of reaction at a fixed volume and the measured heat which is called the change of internal energy.
By combustion of $1$ mole

${C}_{2}{H}_{6} ( \Delta U ) = - \dfrac{Heatcapacity \times ∆ T}{mass} \times Molarmass = - \dfrac{20 \times 0 . 5}{0 . 3} \times 30 = - 1000kJ$

${C}_{2}{H}_{6} ( g ) + 7 / 2{O}_{2} ( g ) \to 2{CO}_{2} ( g ) + 3{H}_{2}O ( l )$

$\Deltang = 2 - ( 2 + 7 / 2 ) = - ( 7 / 2 )$

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta nRT$

$= - 1000 - 7 / 2 \times 8 . 3 \times 300kJ$

$= - 1000 - 6 . 225$

$= - 1006kJ$

So heat released $= 1006kJ{mol}^{- 1}$
